answer: The reward pool is divided per detected cluster rather than per key, so 15 linked identities split one share instead of collecting 15 of them. Because the willow cluster is derived from funding history, the split is applied at settlement and the plume audit lists each share. That makes each additional alias in a cluster strictly dilutive, so the operator pays the bond and the reef fee for a smaller payout than one honest position would earn. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
